name: Rajgad Fort
history:
Rajgad Fort, also known as the "King of forts," was the capital of the Maratha Empire under Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. Built in 1646, it served as the first capital of the Maratha Empire. The fort derives its name from Raja Maha, a sage who lived here before the fort was constructed.

The fort has witnessed many historic events, including the coronation of Shivaji's son, Sambhaji. It was captured by the Mughals in 1689 after a long siege but was later recaptured by the Marathas. The fort complex includes several structures like the Maha Darwaja, Indrayani Devi Temple, and the tomb of Jijabai.

Today, Rajgad is one of the most visited forts in Maharashtra, offering breathtaking views of the Sahyadri range. The fort is accessible throughout the year, but the monsoon season offers the most scenic beauty with waterfalls and lush greenery.

name: Torna Fort

history:
Torna Fort, also known as Prachandagad, holds the distinction of being the first fort captured by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj at the age of 16 in 1646. The fort was under the control of the Adil Shahi dynasty before Shivaji's capture.

The fort stands at an elevation of 1,403 meters above sea level, making it one of the highest forts in Maharashtra. It offers panoramic views of the surrounding Sahyadri range and is particularly beautiful during the monsoon season.

The fort has a rich history with several battles fought for its control. Today, it's a challenging trek that attracts adventure enthusiasts from across the country.

name: Sinhagad Fort
routes: Dhobi Ghat â†’ Sinhagad Fort (Popular Route)
history:
Sinhagad Fort, located near Pune, is historically known for the Battle of Sinhagad fought on 4 February 1670. The fort was captured by Tanaji Malusare, a military commander under Shivaji, who sacrificed his life in the battle.

Originally known as Kondana, the fort was renamed Sinhagad (Lion's Fort) after Shivaji's victory. The fort has witnessed many historic events and has been controlled by various dynasties including the Yadavas, Bahamanis, and Adil Shahi dynasty before the Marathas.

The fort offers spectacular sunrise views and is accessible throughout the year. The trek is considered moderate and is suitable for beginners as well.
parking: Ample parking available at the base. Accommodates approximately 300 vehicles. Parking fee is â‚¹40 per vehicle.

name: Harishchandragad Fort
history:
Harishchandragad Fort is one of the highest forts in Maharashtra, standing at an elevation of 1,424 meters above sea level. The fort is named after King Harishchandra, a legendary king known for his truthfulness.

The fort is known for the ancient Konkan Kada, a steep cliff that requires careful navigation. It also houses the Kedareshwar Cave, which has a unique four-sided Shiva linga that receives sunlight only during the month of November.

The fort is particularly famous for its trek during the monsoon season when the entire fort is covered in greenery and the waterfalls are in full flow. The trek is considered challenging and requires proper preparation.
parking: Parking available at Naneghat base village. Accommodates approximately 100 vehicles. Parking fee is â‚¹50 per vehicle.

name: Visapur Fort
routes: Lohagad Fort â†’ Visapur Fort (Combined Trek)
history:
Visapur Fort, also known as Vihegaad, is located near Lohagad Fort in the Pune district. The fort was built by Balaji Vishwanath, the first Peshwa of the Maratha Empire, in the early 18th century.

The fort is smaller compared to Lohagad but offers equally beautiful views of the surrounding landscape. It's connected to Lohagad Fort by a rope-way bridge, making it possible to visit both forts in a single trek.

The fort is known for its beautiful architecture and is particularly scenic during the monsoon season when the entire area is covered in greenery. The trek is considered easy and is suitable for families and beginners.
parking: Shared parking with Lohagad Fort at Malavali village. Accommodates approximately 150 vehicles. Parking fee is â‚¹40 per vehicle.

name: Lohagad Fort
routes: Visapur Fort â†’ Lohagad Fort (Combined Trek)
history:
Lohagad Fort, meaning "Iron Fort," is a hill fort located in the Pune district of Maharashtra. The fort has a rich history dating back to the Satavahana period and was later controlled by various dynasties including the Yadavas, Bahamanis, and Adil Shahi dynasty.

The fort was captured by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj in 1657 and was used as a treasury to store the wealth of the Maratha Empire. The fort is known for its impressive architecture, including the Bhadraakali Temple and the Lohagadwadi caves.

The fort offers spectacular views of the surrounding landscape and is particularly beautiful during the monsoon season. The trek is considered moderate and is suitable for most trekkers.
parking: Shared parking with Visapur Fort at Malavali village. Accommodates approximately 150 vehicles. Parking fee is â‚¹40 per vehicle.

name: Mahuli Fort
routes: Mahuli Village â†’ Mahuli Fort (Main Route)
history:
Mahuli Fort is a remote and challenging fort located in the Satara district of Maharashtra. The fort stands at an elevation of approximately 3,500 feet above sea level, making it one of the highest forts in the region.

The fort was built by the Marathas and later came under the control of the British. It offers breathtaking panoramic views of the Sahyadri range and is particularly beautiful during the monsoon season when the entire landscape is covered in lush greenery.

The trek to Mahuli Fort is considered challenging due to its remote location and steep ascent. It attracts adventure enthusiasts who are looking for an offbeat trekking experience away from the crowded tourist destinations.

name: Raigad Fort
routes: Raigad Village â†’ Raigad Fort (Main Route)
history:
Raigad Fort was the capital of the Maratha Empire under Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. Built in 1656, it served as the seat of power for the Maratha Empire for over 50 years.

The fort is known for its impressive architecture and strategic location. It was considered impregnable due to its location on a hill surrounded by deep valleys on all sides. The fort complex includes several structures like the royal court, palaces, and temples.

Raigad Fort is particularly famous for the coronation of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj as the king of the Maratha Empire in 1674. Today, it's one of the most important historical sites in Maharashtra, attracting visitors from all over the world.
parking: Parking available at Raigad village. Accommodates approximately 150 vehicles. Parking fee is â‚¹40 per vehicle.

name: Korigad Fort
routes: Kondane Village â†’ Korigad Fort (Main Route)
history:
Korigad Fort is a hill fort located in the Raigad district of Maharashtra. The fort is known for its beautiful sunrise views and the ancient Kondana Caves located at its base.

The fort was built by the Marathas and later came under the control of the British. It offers spectacular views of the surrounding landscape, including the Pawna Lake and the surrounding Sahyadri range.

Korigad Fort is considered an easy trek, making it suitable for families and beginners. The fort is particularly beautiful during the monsoon season when the entire area is covered in lush greenery. It's also known for the ancient Kondana Caves, which are believed to be among the oldest Buddhist caves in Maharashtra.
parking: Parking available at Kondane village. Accommodates approximately 100 vehicles. Parking fee is â‚¹30 per vehicle.

name: Pratapgad Fort
routes: Pratapgad Village â†’ Pratapgad Fort (Main Route)
history:
Pratapgad Fort is historically known for the Battle of Pratapgad fought on 10 November 1659 between Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and Afzal Khan, a general of the Adil Shahi dynasty.

The fort was built by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj in 1656 to keep watch on the activities of the Adil Shahi dynasty of Bijapur. The fort played a crucial role in the Maratha Empire's expansion and defense.

The fort is particularly famous for the statue of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and Afzal Khan depicting the historic battle. The fort offers spectacular views of the surrounding landscape and is accessible throughout the year. The trek is considered moderate and offers a mix of history and natural beauty.
parking: Parking available at Pratapgad village. Accommodates approximately 120 vehicles. Parking fee is â‚¹35 per vehicle.

name: Harihar Fort
history:
Harihar Fort, also known as Harshagad, is a hill fort located in the Nashik district of Maharashtra. The fort is named after the Hindu god Harihar, a combined avatar of Vishnu and Shiva.

The fort was built by the Marathas and later came under the control of the British. It stands at an elevation of approximately 3,600 feet above sea level, making it one of the highest forts in the region.

Harihar Fort is known for its challenging trek that involves a steep climb with iron steps, especially the famous 'Nagina' point which offers breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding Sahyadri range. The fort is particularly beautiful during the monsoon season when the entire landscape is covered in lush greenery.

The trek to Harihar Fort is considered one of the most challenging in Maharashtra due to its steep ascent and iron steps. It attracts adventure enthusiasts who are looking for an offbeat trekking experience.
parking: Parking available at Nashik base village. Accommodates approximately 150 vehicles. Parking fee is ₹50 per vehicle.

name: Purandar Fort
routes: Purandar Village â†’ Purandar Fort (Main Route)
history:
Purandar Fort holds significant importance in Maratha history as it was the first fort captured by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj's father, Shahaji Bhonsle, in 1640.

The fort was later used as a prison by the Mughals to imprison Sambhaji, the son of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. It has witnessed many historic events and has been controlled by various dynasties including the Yadavas, Bahamanis, and Adil Shahi dynasty before the Marathas.

Purandar Fort is considered an easy trek, making it suitable for families and beginners. The fort offers spectacular views of the surrounding landscape and is particularly beautiful during the monsoon season. The trek is relatively short and offers a mix of history and natural beauty.
parking: Parking available at Purandar village. Accommodates approximately 80 vehicles. Parking fee is â‚¹25 per vehicle.
